papers.title: Proof-of-Concept End-to-End EEG-BCI Pipeline for Grasp-and-Release Decoding and Low-Cost Tendon-Driven Actuation
papers.summary: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term motor disability, inspiring research in the design of assistive and rehabilitation technologies that work in situations with limited residual muscle activity. Brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) offer a promising non-muscular pathway to translate brain activity into BCI commands. This paper presents the proof-of-concept end-to-end pipeline for the use of binary grasp-and-release Electroencephalography-Brain Computer Interface (EEG-BCI) decoding in conjunction with low-cost tendon-driven robotic hand actuation. papers.summary: Multi-agent navigation is a fundamental problem in robotics, autonomous vehicles, warehouse automation, traffic management, and other systems in which several autonomous entities must reach individual destinations while sharing limited space. Classical Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) focuses on producing collision-free paths, whereas Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) learns policies through interaction and can adapt to changing agent behavior. papers.title: Gap filling in long-term AOD time series using Iterative Singular Spectrum Analysis at a tropical AERONET site
papers.summary: Abstract Aerosol optical depth (AOD) is widely used in studies related to atmospheric monitoring, climate variability, and air quality, with the Aerosol RObotic NETwork (AERONET) providing high-quality records. However, AERONET AOD time series frequently contain observational gaps associated with cloud cover, especially in tropical regions characterized by strong hydrological seasonality. papers.title: Length of stay and nhi-reimbursed expenditures after robotic-assisted surgery in taiwan: a nationwide population-based study
papers.summary: Population-level evidence comparing robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) with laparoscopic surgery (LS)/video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and open surgery (OS) across multiple procedures from a payer perspective remains limited. This study aimed to compare postoperative length of stay (LOS) and insurer-reimbursed in-hospital expenditures among RAS, LS/VATS, and OS across representative procedures following the expansion of RAS reimbursement in Taiwan. papers.summary: Long-term orbital missions require highly independent life-support systems, maintaining ecological stability under limited external support and subsystem attenuation. Conventional strategies are typically based on fixed threshold rules or deterministic mass-balance models and cannot adapt to disturbances or multi-objective trade-offs between resource safety and environmental load. papers.summary: Dynamic treatment regimes (DTRs) provide a principled framework for optimizing sequential decision-making in domains where decisions must adapt over time in response to individual trajectories, such as healthcare, education, and digital interventions. papers.summary: 컨텍스트 기반 오프라인 메타 강화학습 (Context-based Offline Meta-RL, COMRL)은 정적 데이터만으로 새로운 태스크에 빠르게 적응하는 에이전트를 학습한다. 그러나 기존 방법들은 컨텍스트를 수집하는 행동 정책이 학습 분포와 다르면 정책이 학습된 적 없는 잠재에서 실행되어 성능이 붕괴하고, 이를 보완하는 고정 계수 비관주의는 환경별 튜닝과 과보수화 문제를 낳는다. 본 논문이 제안하는 DELPHI는 잠재 공간을 외삽한 뒤 디코더 앙상블의 합성 롤아웃으로 정책을 학습 분포 밖 잠재에서 미리 단련하되, 롤아웃을 따라 누적한 앙상블 불일치 (정보 드리프트)를 z-점수로 정규화하고 임계 초과분에만 비선형 게이트로 페널티를 부과하여 신뢰도가 낮은 합성 신호를 억제한다. 게이트는 정상 영역에서 페널티를 0으로 두어 분포 내 성능을 보존하고, 롤아웃 구조 파라미터는 환경별로 설정하되 정규화의 스케일 불변성 덕분에 게이트 상수에 한하여 전 환경 단일 값으로 공유되어 환경별 페널티 계수 탐색을 대체한다. papers.title: Curriculum Reinforcement Learning for Robust Autonomous Vehicle Entry in Mixed-Autonomy Roundabouts
papers.summary: Autonomous vehicle (AV) insertion into mixed-autonomy roundabouts is a challenging decision-making problem due to interactions with human-driven vehicles (HDVs), uncertain traffic gaps, and collision risks. This work investigates a curriculum reinforcement learning framework for training a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent to perform robust AV insertion in a simulated roundabout environment using Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO). The framework combines a spatial spawn curriculum with a traffic-composition curriculum that progressively increases the proportion of human-driven vehicles

papers.title: Computer Vision-Based Characterization of Temporal Feeding Dynamic in Group-Housed Dairy Goats
papers.summary: Feeding behavior is closely related to nutrient intake, health, and production performance, yet its temporal dynamics are difficult to quantify in group-housed dairy goats. We developed a computer vision-based framework to characterize feeding dynamics under commercial farm conditions. Video data were collected from 550 Guanzhong dairy goats housed in five pens over three consecutive days. YOLO11, RF-DETR, and RT-DETR were compared for feeding-area goat detection, and temporal feeding features were analyzed to characterize high feeding activity (HFA) and low feeding activity (LFA). papers.summary: HSRPs are designed to make it uniform and to facilitate quick identification of vehicles but the surveillance of vast amounts of traffic manually is expensive and unfeasible. papers.title: The Architecture of Intoxication: Opium Dens, Use of Bodies and New World Orders
papers.summary: Abstract What is the relationship between the experience of intoxication and the built environment in which it occurs? This article reflects on how the materiality of spaces of intoxication offers a lens for exploring the interplay between bodily and psychic experiences and their connection to the emerging world orders. We focus on the architecture of so-called opium dens as largely unexplored historical sites, examining how they shaped consumers and embodied tensions between meaning-making and meaning-erasure.
